'''Kristafer Aaron Wilkes''' (born September 18, 1998)<ref name=usab_bio>{{cite web|title=Kris Wilkes|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/kris-wilkes|website=NBA Draft.net}}</ref> is an American former [[basketball]] player. As a high school senior, he was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was a [[starting lineup|starter]] as a freshman in 2017–18, when he was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team. As a sophomore, he earned second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors in 2019. He went undrafted in the  [[2019 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
As a high school senior in 2017, he was selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref>{{cite news|last1=Halley|first1=Jim|title=Kris Wilkes, with an eye toward the playoffs, gets his McDonald's jersey |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/kris-wilkes-with-an-eye-toward-the-playoffs-gets-his-mcdonalds-jersey |accessdate=July 9, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 22, 2017}}</ref> and was ranked as a consensus five-star prospect in the class of 2017. At the conclusion of his senior year, Wilkes was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] and an Indiana All-Star.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Neddenriep|first1=Kyle|title=Kris Wilkes lost his No. 1 jersey, then helped Indiana All-Stars to a big win |url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/06/11/without-his-no-1-jersey-wilkes-leads-indiana-all-stars-consecutive-win-no-17/370047001/ |accessdate=July 9, 2017|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=June 10, 2017}}</ref>

chose to play for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Five-star recruit Kris Wilkes chooses UCLA over Indiana, Illinois UCLA qualified for the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]], but lost 65–58 to [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]] in the First Four. After starting all previous 32 games entering the tournament, Wilkes did not start the game, sitting out the first five minutes for disciplinary reasons after being late for a team bus earlier in the week.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fenno|first=Nathan|title=UCLA loses to St. Bonaventure in play-in game to the NCAA tournament|date=March 13, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-st-bonaventure-20180313-story.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Rittenberg|first=Adam|title=Bruins sit Kris Wilkes for opening minutes of loss In the [[2018–19 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2018–19]] season opener, Wilkes scored 27 points and added 10 rebounds in a 96–71 win over [[Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball|Purdue Fort Wayne]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA's Kris Wilkes has career night in season-opening blowout|date=November 6, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-purdue-fort-wayne-20181106-story.html|accessdate=November 7, 2018}}</ref> On December 8, 2018, he made a game-winning three-pointer with 0.9 seconds remaining in a 65–62 win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA stuns Notre Dame on injured Kris Wilkes' last-second 3-pointer|date=December 8, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/12/08/injured-kris-wilkes-stuns-notre-dame-with-last-second-3-pointer/|accessdate=December 11, 2018}}</ref> On January 26, 2019, he scored a career-high 34 points on 12-of-16 shooting from the field to help UCLA end a three-game losing streak in a 90–69 win over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=Kris Wilkes scores career high as UCLA men's basketball ends losing streak|date=January 26, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/26/kris-wilkes-scores-career-high-as-ucla-mens-basketball-ends-losing-streak/|accessdate=January 29, 2019}}</ref> On the road against [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], Wilkes had 27 points and 10 rebounds to help the Bruins win 75–67 in overtime and end a three-game losing streak. "[Wilkes is] our best player, and that’s the way he's supposed to play", said interim coach [[Murry Bartow]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA struggles to keep ahead of last-place Cal in 75-67 overtime win|date=February 13, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-cal-20190213-story.html|accessdate=February 15, 2019}}</ref> He finished the season as the Bruins leading scoring (17.4),<ref name=nguyen_03272019>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA guard Kris Wilkes declares for NBA draft with agent|date=March 27, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/27/ucla-guard-kris-wilkes-declares-for-nba-draft-with-agent/|accessdate=March 29, 2019}}</ref> and was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA's Jaylen Hands, Kris Wilkes named All-Pac-12 second team|date=March 11, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/11/uclas-jaylen-hands-kris-wilkes-named-all-pac-12-second-team/|accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref> While his scoring increased by almost four points per game from his freshman year, his [[field goal percentage]] dropped from 44.1 to 43.3.<ref name=nguyen_03272019/> After the season, which UCLA finished 17–16 and failed to qualify for the NCAA tournament, Wilkes declared again for the NBA draft.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA's Kris Wilkes announces he's headed to the NBA|date=March 27, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-kris-wilkes-20190327-story.html|accessdate=March 29, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After not showing dramatic improvement as a UCLA sophomore, Wilkes went undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA's Jaylen Hands headed to Brooklyn Nets after going 56th in NBA draft|date=June 20, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/06/20/uclas-jaylen-hands-headed-to-brooklyn-nets-after-going-56th-in-nba-draft/|accessdate=June 22, 2019}}</ref> He was expected to sign a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New York Knicks]] after general manager [[Scott Perry (basketball)|Scott Perry]] talked about him while introducing their 2019 draft picks.<ref name=popper_07022019/><ref name=Berman_09082019>{{cite news|last=Berman|first=Marc|title=Knicks summoning Kris Wilkes for new physical in last hope|date=September 8, 2019|newspaper=New York What to know about 2-way player Kris Wilkes|date=June 24, 2019|website=NorthJersey.com|url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2019/06/24/new-york-knicks-what-know-2-way-player-kris-wilkes/1544476001/|accessdate=September 25, 2019}}</ref> However, Wilkes was unable to play in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] due to a severe, undisclosed illness,<ref name=popper_07022019>{{cite news|last=Popper|first=Steve|title=RJ Barrett keeps his focus on learning, trying to help Knicks|date=July 2, 2019|newspaper=Newsday|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/rj-barrett-knicks-1.33304294|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703120745/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/rj-barrett-knicks-1.33304294|url-status=dead|archive-date=July York Daily News|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-ivan-rabb-power-forward-20191023-4vfbe3o52nf3zlezunbum6vctm-story.html|accessdate=October 25, 2019}}</ref> and the Knicks signed [[Ivan Rabb]] with their remaining two-way slot.<ref name=bondy_10232019/> 
Wilkes later described the illness as [[acute disseminated encephalomyelitis]], a rare autoimmune disease.<ref>{{cite news | url =  https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/23/sports/basketball/kris-wilkes-ucla-nba.html | author = David Gardner | title = His N.B.A. Dream Was Right There. Then He Couldn't Move His Legs. | work = The New York Times | date = October 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/09/08/where-kris-wilkes-2017-indiana-mr-basketball-ucla-bruins-origynsport-north-central-indianapolis-nba/8169017002/|title='Where is Kris Wilkes?' 2017 Mr. Basketball working way back after auto-immune disease.|work=Indianapolis Star|first=Kyle|last= Neddenriep|date=October 23, 2021}}</ref>

In 2024, he was invited to work out with the [[Indiana Pacers]]. They asked him to participate in their summer training camp, though he was not given an [[NBA Summer League]] contract.<ref>{{cite news|first=Dustin|last=Dopirak|title=5 years after Kris Wilkes was told he'd never play in NBA, Indy native works out for Pacers|date=July 10, 2024|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2024/07/10/kris-wilkes-has-eye-opening-experience-in-pacers-summer-camp/74341083007/|access-date=October 27, 2025}}</ref> On October 27, Wilkes joined the [[Indiana Mad Ants]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mad Ants Basketball|title=our 2024-25 training camp roster 🐜🔥|number=1850621766915539218|user=TheMadAnts|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on November 6.<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Indiana Mad Ants Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Indiana-Mad-Ants/68/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 7, 2024}}</ref>
